Question 22 (Part A, multiple choice).

Given the following standard reference values at $25\,^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $100\,\mathrm{kPa}$, which of the following combination of thermodynamic values describes a reaction that is endothermic and spontaneous at $2000\,^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$? Assume enthalpy and entropy values are not temperature dependent.

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c} & \Delta H^\circ\ (\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}) & \Delta S^\circ\ (\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}) & \Delta G^\circ\ (\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}) \\ \hline \text{A)} & 217.0 & 115.0 & 182.7 \\ \text{B)} & -230.0 & -11.0 & -226.7 \\ \text{C)} & 52.0 & 10.0 & 49.0 \\ \text{D)} & -363.0 & 249.0 & -437.2 \\ \text{E)} & 268.6 & -88.0 & 294.8 \end{array}$$

Question 2 (Part B, extended response). Finding Equilibrium (Choice)

What is chemical equilibrium and what is its importance in the study of chemistry? Using examples of equilibria with which you are familiar, explain the term "dynamic equilibrium" and explain how equilibrium involves opposing processes that occur at the same rate. Using chemical equilibrium systems, explain how buffers work and what the Common Ion Effect is. Explain how to use Le Chatelier's Principle in a variety of ways to manipulate equilibria and how to precisely predict the equilibrium concentrations of reactants and products given the equilibrium constant for a reaction and initial concentration of reactants and products.

Topic B

B1. The elements ${}_{14}\mathrm{Si}$ and ${}_{17}\mathrm{Cl}$ are given.
a. Write the electronic structure of their atoms (distribution of electrons in subshells) in the ground state.
b. Justify which of these two elements has the greater first ionisation energy ($E_{i1}$).
c. Write the Lewis electron formula of the compound $\ce{SiCl4}$.

B2. An aqueous solution of a weak acid HA (Solution Δ) is given. Will the degree of ionisation of the acid increase, decrease or remain constant if
a. water is added to solution Δ?
Justify your answer.
b. an amount of the solid salt NaA is added to solution Δ without change of volume?
Justify your answer.
The temperature remains constant in both cases.

B3. Copy into your answer booklet the following chemical equations, correctly completed:
a. $\ce{(CH3)2C=O + H2 ->}$
b. $\nu\,\ce{CH2=CH-CH=CH2 ->[\text{polymerisation}]}$
c. $\ce{CH3CH2CHCl2 + 2NaOH ->[\text{alcohol}]}$

Topic D

We have aqueous solutions of $\ce{CH3COONa}$ $0.1\ \mathrm{M}$ (solution A) and $\ce{NaF}$ $1\ \mathrm{M}$ (solution B).

D1. Calculate the pH of solution A.

D2. How many mL of $\ce{H2O}$ must we add to 10 mL of solution A in order to change its pH by one unit?

D3. How many mL of $\ce{HCl}$ solution $0.01\ \mathrm{M}$ must we add to 10 mL of solution A in order to obtain a buffer solution with pH = 5?

D4. 10 mL of solution A are mixed with 40 mL of solution B, giving 50 mL of solution Γ. Calculate the pH of solution Γ.

Given:
• All solutions are at a temperature $\theta = 25\,^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, $K_{\mathrm{a}(\ce{CH3COOH})} = 10^{-5}$, $K_{\mathrm{a}(\ce{HF})} = 10^{-4}$, $K_\mathrm{w} = 10^{-14}$
• The data of the problem allow the usual approximations.

Question 3 (Part A).

For the organic compounds A, B, Γ, Δ and E, all with a straight carbon chain, the following physical constants are given:

$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|} \hline & \textbf{m.p.}\ ({}^{\circ}\mathrm{C}) & \textbf{b.p.}\ ({}^{\circ}\mathrm{C}) \\ \hline \textbf{Alkane A} & -130 & 36 \\ \hline \textbf{Alkane B} & -138 & 0 \\ \hline \textbf{Alkane Γ} & -188 & -42 \\ \hline \textbf{Alcohol Δ} & -127 & 97 \\ \hline \textbf{Organic acid E} & 63 & 350 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

(a) State the physical state of the compounds A, B, Γ, Δ and E (at a temperature of $25\,{}^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$).
(b) Which of the alkanes has the longest carbon chain? Explain your answer briefly.
(c) Alkane B and alcohol Δ have similar molar masses. Explain briefly why they have different boiling points.

Question 5 (Part A).

The following information is given about compounds A, B, Γ, X and Ψ.
I. Compound A is the organic product of the reaction of o-$\ce{ClC6H4CHCl2}$ with hot aqueous potassium hydroxide solution.
II. Compound B is the organic product of the addition reaction of hydrogen bromide to 4-methylhexa-1,4-diene, $\ce{CH2=CHCH2C(CH3)=CHCH3}$, in the presence of UV radiation.
III. Compound Γ, which shows no stereoisomerism, has the molecular formula $\ce{C5H9ClO}$. Its reaction with concentrated aqueous sodium hydroxide solution gives two (2) organic products, X and Ψ, of which compound X has the molecular formula $\ce{C5H12O2}$.

Write the structural formulas of the organic compounds A, B, Γ, X and Ψ.

Problem 1-3: An experiment to do yourself

In an experiment, $10\,\mathrm{mL}$ of an $\ce{Fe^{3+}}$ solution and $30\,\mathrm{mL}$ of an $\ce{SCN^-}$ solution are combined. Both solutions have the same, not too high concentration; otherwise the effect is marginal.
Observation 1: A red solution is formed.

A portion of the red solution is diluted to ten times its volume.
Observation 2: The solution turns red-brown.

To one portion of the diluted solution a little solid iron(III) chloride is added.
Observation 3: The solution turns red.

To another portion of the diluted solution a little solid ammonium thiocyanate is added.
Observation 4: The solution turns red.

a) Interpret the four observations.

b) Explain why parts 3 and 4 of the experiment support the explanation of observation 2.

Problem 3-2

$1.004\,\mathrm{g}$ of a metal chloride ($\ce{MCl_y}$, $1 \le y \le 4$) is slowly heated in air to red heat. This forms $0.594\,\mathrm{g}$ of a solid that contains the same mass of metal as the original metal chloride, but no chlorine any more.

a) Identify the substances and write an equation for the reaction that takes place on heating. Check whether there is more than one solution.

Besides the composition of a compound, the structure of its molecule or ion is also of interest. Predictions can be made for this by means of the electron-pair repulsion model (VSEPR).
The following sulfur compounds are chosen as examples:
$\ce{SO2}$, $\ce{SO3(g)}$, $\ce{SOF2}$, $\ce{SO4^{2-}}$, $\ce{SF4}$, $\ce{SOF4}$, $\ce{SF6}$.

b) Draw the structures of these species together with the lone pairs on sulfur.
Name the geometric structure of the compounds or ions (e.g. linear, square pyramid, etc.).

Problem B5 (Part B, optional). Reactions of organic compounds

Below are shown schemes of reactions taking place with the participation of organic compounds.

Task: Complete the schemes by giving the formulae of the reaction products:

1.

$$\mathrm{R}^{\ast)}\text{-}\ce{CHO + Cu(OH)2 ->[\Delta T]}$$

2.

$$\ce{R-CHO + H2N-NHC6H5 ->}$$

3.

$$\ce{R-CHO + 2 C2H5OH ->[H+]}$$

4.

$$\ce{R-CH2CHO + C6H5CHO ->[OH-]}$$

5.

$$\ce{R-NH2 + C6H5COCl ->}$$

6.

$$\ce{ArH + C6H5COCl ->[AlCl3]}$$

7.

$$\ce{R-COOH + B2H6 ->[THF]}$$

8.

$$\ce{R-CONHMe + LiAlH4 ->}$$

9.

$$\ce{R2C=O + LiAlH4 ->}$$

10.

$$\ce{Me2C=O + I2 ->[OH-]}$$

$^{\ast)}$ abbreviations used in the schemes:

R – hydrocarbon residue,

$\mathrm{C_6H_5}$ – phenyl group,

Ar – residue of an aromatic hydrocarbon,

THF – tetrahydrofuran,

Me – methyl group,

$\Delta\mathrm{T}$ – heating.

Problem A1 (Part A, compulsory). Acid-base reactions

$100\,\mathrm{cm^3}$ of an $\ce{NH4Cl}$ solution of concentration $0.2\,\mathrm{mol/dm^3}$ was prepared. To this solution, $10\,\mathrm{cm^3}$ portions of $\ce{NaOH}$ solution of concentration $1\,\mathrm{mol/dm^3}$ were added in three successive portions.

Task: Calculate the pH of the $\ce{NH4Cl}$ solution before the addition of $\ce{NaOH}$ and after the introduction of each successive portion of this base solution. Write the corresponding reaction equations in ionic form.

Acid dissociation constant of $\ce{NH4+}$: $K_\mathrm{a} = 6.3\cdot10^{-10}$

Problem 3. A way to dissolve silver

The potential $E_1$ of the silver electrode was determined in a solution of $\ce{AgNO3}$ with a concentration of 0.0100 M. After that, 0.0170 g of $\ce{NH3}$ was added to $10.0\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of the solution. In the resulting solution, the potential of the Ag electrode was different from $E_1$ by 0.285 V. The temperature of the solution was 25 °C.

$\ce{NH3}$ forms a complex in $\ce{AgNO3}$ solution according to the reaction $\ce{Ag+ + 2NH3 <=> [Ag(NH3)2]+}$. Calculate the equilibrium constant of the above reaction.

Problem 3. Silver energy

The EMF of a silver-zinc cell $\ce{Zn}\,|\,\ce{ZnSO4}(\mathrm{l})\,||\,\ce{AgNO3}(\mathrm{l})\,|\,\ce{Ag}$ is 1.562 V if the concentrations of the solutions are 1 M at $T = 25\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

a) Write the equations of the reactions in the whole cell and at single electrodes if current is taken from the cell.

b) Calculate the EMF of the cell after 20 days of running at 0.050 A.

Problem 4. [Combustion analysis of a gaseous hydrocarbon]

$15\,\mathrm{cm^3}$ of a gaseous hydrocarbon $\ce{C_xH_y}$ are mixed with $120\,\mathrm{cm^3}$ oxygen and ignited. After the reaction the burned gases are shaken with concentrated aqueous KOH solution. A part of the gases is completely absorbed while $67.5\,\mathrm{cm^3}$ gases remain. It has the same temperature and pressure as the original unburned mixture.

4.1 What is the composition of the remaining gas? Explain.

4.2 How large is the change in the amount of substance per mole of a hydrocarbon $\ce{C_xH_y}$ when this is burned completely?

4.3 What is the chemical formula of the hydrocarbon used for the experiment? Give the steps of the calculation.

Problem 6. [Hydrogen iodide equilibrium]

The equilibrium constant of the reaction $\ce{H2 + I2 <=> 2 HI}$ is at $600\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ equal to $70.0$.

Problems:

6.1 How much iodine (in %) is converted till the equilibrium is reached if the reactants are mixed in:

a) $1:1$ molar ratio at $600\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$;

b) $2:1$ molar ratio at $600\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ (the amount of hydrogen is twice as great as that of iodine).

6.2 How many moles of hydrogen should be mixed with one mole of iodine when $99\,\%$ of iodine is to be converted to hydrogen iodide till the equilibrium is reached at $600\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$?

Problem 1. Equilibrium constant

Answer the following questions using the standard potential, $E^\circ$, values given in the table.

$$\begin{array}{l|c} \text{Half reaction} & E^\circ/\mathrm{V}\ (298\ \mathrm{K}) \\ \hline \ce{Sn^{2+} + 2e- -> Sn} & -0.14 \\ \ce{Sn^{4+} + 2e- -> Sn^{2+}} & +0.15 \\ \ce{Hg2^{2+} + 2e- -> 2Hg} & +0.79 \\ \ce{Hg2Cl2 + 2e- -> 2Hg + 2Cl-} & +0.27 \end{array}$$

a) Calculate the equilibrium constant, $K$, for the following reaction at 298 K

$$\ce{Sn(s) + Sn^{4+}(aq) <=> 2Sn^{2+}(aq)}$$

b) Calculate the solubility, $S$, of $\ce{Hg2Cl2}$ in water at 298 K (units for $S$, $\mathrm{mol\,kg^{-1}}$). The mercury cation in the aqueous phase is $\ce{Hg2^{2+}}$.

c) Calculate the voltage, $E^\circ$, of a fuel cell by using the following reaction involving two electrons.

$$\ce{H2(g) + 1/2 O2(g) -> H2O(l)} \qquad \Delta_r G^\circ = -237.1\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$$

Problem 20. Drug kinetics

The absorption of a drug by an organism often follows simple kinetics though the mechanism is very complicated. Consider a drug delivered orally in a common capsule. Let $[\mathrm{A}]_\mathrm{s}$ be its concentration in the stomach and assume that the rate of its introduction into the blood stream is first order with respect to this $[\mathrm{A}]_\mathrm{s}$. Also assume that the rate by which the drug is metabolized or removed from the blood stream is proportional to its concentration in the blood, $[\mathrm{A}]_\mathrm{b}$. Give the plot of $[\mathrm{A}]_\mathrm{s}$ as a function of time and write the equation representing $\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{A}]_\mathrm{b}/\mathrm{d}t$. After one hour 75% of $[\mathrm{A}]_\mathrm{s}$ have been removed from the stomach. What percentage of the initial $[\mathrm{A}]_\mathrm{s}$ will remain in the stomach two hours after taking the drug?

Practical problem 2. [Qualitative analysis of substances in numbered test tubes] [printed as PROBLEM 2 (Practical); no points or weight are printed in the source]

By means of available reagents and facilities perform a qualitative analysis of the substances given in numbered test tubes and write down their chemical formulas.

Give 10 equations of the chemical reactions by which the substances were proved:

5 equations for reactions of precipitation,

2 equations for reactions connected with release of a gas,

3 equations for redox reactions.

Practical problem 2. [Composition of a formic acid–ethanol mixture after esterification] [printed as PROBLEM 2 (Practical); no points or weight are printed in the source]

On June 10th, a mixture of formic acid with an excess of ethanol was prepared. This mixture was kept in a closed vessel for approximately one month. Determine quantitatively the composition of the mixture on the day of the competition, using only reagents and facilities available on the laboratory desk. Calculate the amounts of the acid and ethanol in per cent by mass which were initially mixed together.
